notes: THE DOCUMENTED TARGET FOR A CELL THAT IS NOT RECORDABLE HERE. All three pillars are green — agent=yes, daemon=full, driver=ready — but the recipe is applicable:false with record_blocked:upstream, so these phases are the spec a recording WILL be validated against once the plan is upgraded, not something verified today. WHY THIS CELL IS NOT FROZEN LIKE ITS FIVE SIBLINGS: claudecode, codex, gemini-cli, kiro-cli and pi all landed daemon=incapable on this row because their provider is a startup choice and provider identity never reaches the transcript. Copilot 1.0.77 breaks both halves. app.js's handleNativeRateLimitedTurn has a promptless `action==="switch_auto"` branch that emits session.info{infoType:auto_mode_switch,"Rate limited. Switching to auto mode to continue."}, calls applyModelChange(cC,{cause:"rate_limit_auto_switch"}) with cC="auto", and RETURNS {action:"continue"} — the same turn continues under the fallback. That is the scenario's process steps 2-5 in one expression, and the vendor's own ModelChangeData.cause schema text calls it "the reason the change happened, when not user-initiated". WHAT IRRLICHT SEES, AND FROM WHICH PERSISTED EVENT: the failover's model change rides session.model_change, which — unlike assistant.turn_retry, model.call_failure and auto_mode_switch.requested/completed, all four of which are ephemeral:{const:true} and were found ZERO times across 6 local session dirs / 13 turns — IS persisted (5 lines observed on disk). The copilot parser's existing arm (parser.go L88-90) reads newModel into ModelName and marks the event Skip=true, which delivers acceptance bullets (a) ModelName changes and (b) no state flicker in the same two lines; assistant.turn_end delivers (c). No adapter change is needed, which is why this is full and not bug. THE ONE SUBTLETY THE PHASES BELOW ENCODE: newModel on this path is the literal placeholder "auto", not a resolved id, so ModelName reads "auto" from the failover until the next assistant.message re-stamps the concrete fallback. A turn that CONTINUES necessarily emits one, so bullet (c) still holds — but the model is asserted only after turn_end, never inside the failover window. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: the retry attempts, the provider status code, and the user-prompted variant of the switch, because all four witnessing events are ephemeral by the vendor's design; and the cause field itself, because the parser discards it — meaning this transcript's signature is observationally identical to a /model switch (5.3). No acceptance bullet mentions any of those. observations.model is UNPINNED: the fallback is whatever the auto-router picks at failover time and no string can be pinned at assess time. WHY IT CANNOT BE DRIVEN HERE: the switch target is "auto" and this account can ONLY be on auto — 5-3 live-verified that every concrete model id is refused with 'only Auto mode is available on your plan' — so there is no pinned premium model to be rate-limited off and the switch_auto branch is structurally unreachable. Unblocking is billing (individual model access) + real quota exhaustion + continueOnAutoMode:true; the rig's BYOK mock-openai-429 is NOT a substitute, because hasByokProvider is an explicit input to the branch decision.

text: The copilot session appears in ready. Anchored UNPINNED to start: events.jsonl is only written at the first prompt, so the 1s process scanner may mint a transient proc-<PID> row first. session.start is Skip=true — a session coming into existence is not activity.
The single long prompt opens the turn → working (user.message → user_message). This is the last user action in the recording; everything the scenario asserts happens with no further input.

The primary model rate-limits and the CLI fails over WITHOUT asking: a real session.model_change{cause:'rate_limit_auto_switch', previousModel:<pinned premium model>, newModel:'auto'} line is written into events.jsonl, alongside session.info{infoType:'auto_mode_switch'}. The parser marks model_change Skip=true (parser.go L88-90), so no state machinery fires — the session stays working across the switch with no flicker to ready and none to waiting. This is acceptance bullet (b), asserted against an actual transcript event rather than against silence. ModelName changes here without user action — bullet (a) — though it changes to the placeholder 'auto' first; the concrete fallback arrives in the next phase.

THE PHASE THAT SEPARATES THIS CELL FROM ITS FROZEN SIBLINGS: at least one assistant.message follows the failover inside the SAME turn, carrying the concrete fallback model id, and the session is still working. handleNativeRateLimitedTurn returns {action:'continue'} rather than aborting — so unlike scenario 2.14's error-aborted turn (which writes assistant.turn_end and then session.error), no turn boundary is crossed at the failover. parseAssistantMessage re-stamps ModelName from the placeholder 'auto' to the real fallback label.

assistant.turn_end settles working→ready on the same session id — acceptance bullet (c). SessionMetrics.ModelName is a concrete Copilot model label: NOT 'unknown', and NOT the placeholder 'auto' the failover momentarily set. TotalTokens > 0 from the turn's live assistant.message outputTokens increments. The session never enters waiting.

exit_clean shuts the CLI down; session.shutdown lands the cumulative usage block (input tokens have no live signal and arrive only here) and the session's final state is ready. modelMetrics is expected to carry TWO keys on this cell — the pinned primary and the fallback — which makes it the one copilot recording that can trigger the 5-1 drainPendingContribution tail risk: if TotalTokens under-reports the input side, that caveat is confirmed and promotes to a daemon bug.
